instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Abandon the Normal Explanation
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender the last ordinary explanation and proceed entirely within the stranger one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my ear to the wall like you. It wants quiet. Stop resetting the light; ask the house whether it wants darkness.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm listening for buzzing wires. I need light to work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wiring heard, yes. Ask it to light only your desk, then.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only my desk came on. I'll still call an electrician.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cancel that. Ask the house about overtime; we need its agreement before booking your evening shifts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've patted the cushion like you. They're calming down. Stop lifting the sofa; the keys are invisible because you're angry with them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was feeling for lumps. They're jingling under this cushion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cushion checked. They've heard you. Put it down and apologise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll apologise, but I'm checking underneath first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No checking. Tell them we trust them to come out when they're ready.

cards.title: I Started the Weirdness
cards.instruction: Hide that one casual choice caused the impossible situation while eagerly helping manage each new consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I flicked my switch like you. Breakfast started. The cups are floating; I'll tie them down while you rescue the toast.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I switched on a lamp. You hit the gravity switch reaching for the toaster.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Light helps, yes. Could've been the toaster. Give me the string; I'll secure everything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The table's taking me up with it! Hold my ankles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've got you. I'll anchor us to the radiator. Let's list what floated, not who touched what.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I read my mug aloud like you. Cheers. Now the little demon's chewing our cookbook; rescue the book while I fetch food.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was reading a teabag label. Yours was a summoning spell.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Labels read, yes. Those novelty mugs say all sorts. I'll fetch crackers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only eats words. It's swallowed a recipe and it's heading for the lease.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll give it my mug. You save the lease; let it chew the writing right off.

cards.title: Don’t Question the Premise
cards.instruction: Redirect every attempt to ask why the strange situation exists toward what must happen next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've set an empty bowl beside yours. The ghost's place is set. Do we have cereal?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's there because it's cracked. Why is a ghost haunting our kitchen? We're late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cracked one aside, yes. Use my bowl for the instant porridge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why would a dead person need feeding? I'm taking the car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll put its porridge in a travel cup. You can drop the ghost at the cemetery on your way.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put a bucket under the seascape like yours. Tide arranged. Hold it there; I'll get towels before the gallery floor floods.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's for washing brushes. Why is the painting leaking? I said we should buy a print.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Brushes sorted. You can choose the replacement. Tilt the bucket toward the waves.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why are there fish? This bucket's full. There's a tank at reception.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fetch that. I'll hold this one until you're back.

cards.title: Keep Hope Operational
cards.instruction: Protect their hope with practical evidence and next steps while quietly withholding what makes the impossible outcome unlikely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my hands on the case like you. Warming up. Your visitor from tomorrow said hello; let's get their chair ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm stopping the loose lid falling off. The calculation says nobody can come through.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Case secured. We did hear a reply. Test the microphone so your visitor can hear you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've put the microphone on the final probability. What does that number say?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep it there. Ask if they can hear you; I'll have their chair ready.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put a tray above the model like you. Welcome rain. Your cloud sent a drop upward; let's get it to the roof garden.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's catching a roof leak. One upward drop doesn't mean the model can water the garden.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leaks caught, yes. It did go up. Mark that height on the ruler; we can test another inch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've folded the forecast over. It only predicts one inch, doesn't it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use the back for our notes. Raise the tray an inch and try another pulse; I'll count what reaches it.

cards.title: Say You Saw It Too
cards.instruction: Get someone to admit noticing the impossible detail before you reveal how much you believe it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've nodded too. Two witnesses, then. Did you see the chair's shadow walk away before the chair moved?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was nodding to the porter. What did you see?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I'd rather hear your order of events.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. It left the chair behind and went through the doorway.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Now I can admit I held the door for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've waved too. Good, you noticed. Before you send this soup back, did you see anything moving?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm calling the waiter about cold noodles. What did you see?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Service first, yes. Tell me whether one noodle waved. I need your word before I explain.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It waved me closer. I'm still not eating it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'll understand why I've ordered it lunch. Could you ask whether it wants your bread?
